entries.topic: The partition plan and the hill country

claims.text: Under the UNSCOP majority plan the Arab state was to comprise western Galilee, the hill country of Samaria and Judea (excluding Jerusalem) and the coastal plain from Isdud to the Sinai frontier; the Jewish state eastern Galilee, the Jezreel Valley, most of the coastal plain and the Negev; each state in three sections linked at two crossing points; Jerusalem under UN trusteeship.

Jewish buyers legally owned about 5.67% of the Mandate's land on 1 April 1945 and 6.6% by the end of 1947; state domain was 46%; by 1948 Jewish farmers cultivated 425,450 dunams and Arab farmers 5,484,700.

The West Bank covers about 5,655 km² (other figures 5,628–5,640); the 1947 plan assigned it to the proposed Arab state; Transjordan captured it in 1948 and annexed it in 1950; Israel captured it with East Jerusalem in June 1967; about 2.75 million Palestinians and over 670,000 settlers (about 220,000 in East Jerusalem), reportedly around 750,000 settlers by 2026; Area C is about 61% of the land and holds about 4% of Palestinians.
Deir Yassin 9 Apr 1948: Irgun and Lehi, with Haganah/Palmach support; about 100–110 killed (Morris; Birzeit study 107); contemporary reports 254.
IPS: the Jewish state received about two-thirds of the coast, including Haifa, Tel Aviv and the fertile lowland plains.

Lydda July 1948: Morris citing Palmach history ~250 dead after Arab Legion armoured incursion and firefight; Rabin gave two versions of Ben-Gurion's response; Allon denied asking; Gelber attributes the decision to Allon; Morris: march deaths 'a handful and perhaps dozens'.
Kfar Etzion 13 May 1948: overrun by Arab Legion and local irregulars; about 127 defenders killed, some after surrendering; other bloc settlements surrendered next day, prisoners to Jordan.
